name: dwg_convert
description: DWG -> DXF conversion and its completeness check (vpt/dwg_convert.py, tools/dwg_convert.py). Every value is a starting value: check it against your converter.
converter_route_note: auto = the ODA File Converter when it is installed (oda_candidates, or ODAFileConverter on PATH), else LibreDWG from converter_nix_shell. oda / nix / path force one route. A route that cannot run is could-not-tell: there is no switch to another route after a failure.
oda_launch_note: How the ODA File Converter (a Qt GUI app) is started: offscreen = QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen (no window; needs the offscreen Qt plugin, which the macOS app does not bundle), background = macOS 'open -W -g -j -n' (hidden, not brought to front; no converter exit code, success is judged from the written files), direct = the plain binary (a window can appear).
converter_nix_note: nix/libredwg.nix rev 'release' = LibreDWG 0.14. The 0.13.x in nixpkgs has been seen to write a DXF that stops after the BLOCKS section while exiting 0; the completeness check below catches that whatever the exit code.

allowed_messages.reason: LibreDWG 0.14 logs this while decoding block attribute records (ATTRIB); the attribute is still written. Accepted only if the 'attribs' verification holds on the file at hand: every INSERT whose block defines ATTDEFs carries as many ATTRIBs, and the ATTRIBs ezdxf reads equal the ATTRIB markers in the DXF.

allowed_messages_note: Reviewed allow-list: a converter line matching unsupported_patterns makes the result could-not-tell unless an entry here accepts it. Every entry has a reason; an entry with 'verify' is re-checked on every run and its result (verified / failed / not verified) is reported with the lines it accepted. A failed verification makes the result could-not-tell again.

completeness.note: Checked on the DXF as written, independent of the converter's exit code. A DXF without EOF, ENTITIES or OBJECTS is cut off: FAIL.
